newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Polifin polymer prices to rise 7-12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polifin polymer prices to rise 7-12 pct.

text.p: South African plastics and chemical producer, Polifin Ltd, said on Monday it would implement price increases of between seven and 12 percent for polyethylene and PVC polymers over the next two months.
Polifin said in a statement this will move prices closer to those of competitive imported material and follows a six month period of stable local prices.
It said world prices for polyethylene and PVC decreased by 35 percent and 50 percent respectively during the latter half of 1995 and the group followed the trend in order to be competitive.
"Prices have recovered over the last year and although the increases have placed pressure on the plastics converting industry, the prices in real terms are still below those of 1995," Polifin said.
Polymer commodity prices in South Africa would continue to be influenced by the dynamics of world markets as a resullt of the opening up of the local economy in recent years.
The international supply availability over the next three to four years was forecast to get easier, with the result that world prices were expected to trend gradually downwards.
"Polifin will price competitively in line with these trends," the group said.
